entry_points.text: Single dispatch syncs caps, emits one-time acquire when preempt present, prefers previous with slice, then local backlog, then scheduler dispatch, with keep-last fallback and immediate scan; needs runqueue lock, brackets callbacks and may drop and reacquire it.

Scheduler dispatch tries global first, honors bypass-only or periodic hosting when enabled, gates on operation presence and online marking, loops invoking dispatch and flushing with rechecks, bounding iterations with deferred kick and ending with final bypass attempt under runqueue lock.

Next install stamps start, notifies running, clears runnable, applies slice updates and maintains tick-stop and load with nohz for infinite versus finite slices; class switch releases at most once when preempt enabled and next above extension; previous bumps kick counter, ends slice with rescue exception, notifies stopping and re-marks runnable when queued.
Normal pick delegates without forcing extension work while server pick forces it only when subsystem active, otherwise yielding no candidate.
Tick refreshes accounting, forces expiry while bypassing, else invokes optional tick and reschedules when slice empty; object release queues deferred teardown so final drop may occur in any context.

exports.text: Move one eligible task from a named shared queue into a given runqueue local queue with retry on remote races; global variant resolves the node queue and delegates plainly; local and bypass identities differ.

Drain staged requests in cursor order with finalization, accounting count and resetting cursor; sync pending capabilities under runqueue lock unless unsupported or empty, draining privately, recomputing sets, notifying and managing renotify and revocation.

Rescue helpers share names with empty or always-decline fallbacks; flush needs runqueue lock, ends occupancy, returns tasks locally and disarms timer; keep declines without slice, queued marking or when bypass active, else installs slice.

Wakeup selection keeps previous CPU for exec and bypass, else scheduler selector then default idle selector; default uses scratch masks with locality fallback under preemption-off and read-side protection; group helper returns stored pointer or null.

hazards.text: Queue destruction refuses non-empty queues, unlinks from lookup, invalidates identifier and defers freeing under RCU plus queue lock; scheduler teardown runs after inactivity covering sync, timer, mask, object, kick, bypass, shard, queue, hash and final free; bypass assumes no new deferrals except ecaps discard which waits.

Consumption stalls on contended queues or retry races, bounded by exiting non-bypass queues while aborting; ineligible production traps dispatch, bounded by iteration limit with deferred kick; holder races fail and retry; sequence mismatch, foreign ownership and failed claims abandon silently.

invariants.text: Remote unlink records holder, drops queue lock before exchanging runqueue locks, then validates; success moves locally else restores lock for retry; moves forbid local source, use global fallback when remote disallowed, never hold two runqueue locks.

Balance queues work only when pending under runqueue lock; bypass is nonzero depth; membership and stay checks have unconditional variants; runqueue flags cover balance, dispatch scope, online, tick and renotify with keep, local and none verdicts.

Effective caps scan ordinals testing container membership and add implied bits where preempt implies enqueue plus immediate and enqueue implies immediate; inactive CPUs discard syncs unchanged; variant without sub-hierarchy is empty.

Preempt reasons are stop, deadline, realtime, unknown; sliced tasks stay at local head outside bypass, immediate ones return marked; higher-class preemption adds last notice when task may stay; dead needs dead plus off-processor; affinity notifies only when enabled.

Idle search falls back through previous, siblings, group, node and wider nodes with unrestricted fast path; claiming clears wholly-idle groups even on failure to avoid livelock; no-node variant fails; operation calls record target with warnings; peek returns head or absence.
No-core-scheduling variant reports no work; online marks extension online while offline clears it, flushes rescue and requeues non-local tasks when inactive; wake runs deferred work.

Stall walk holds runqueue lock with interrupts saved, blaming drainer except local queues; watchdog probes online processors with rescheduling, stops after first stall and requeues unless disabled; weight ignored when dead or disabled else converts to group scale.

Queue teardown checks emptiness then orders release via interrupt work to callback to free; group init walks ancestor-first recording association, teardown descendant-first clearing it; arena is identifier-only with scratch plus shared masks; shard release tolerates nulls; presence counts non-root only; dumping holds dump lock, emits stalled first with truncation and trace mirroring.

locks.text: Sync waiter drops runqueue lock and enables interrupts while spinning, advances progress to avoid cycles, clears satisfied members until empty, and exits immediately on foreign processor.
Group serialization nests global exclusion with group write lock and releases in reverse, with empty variants; root lookup returns hierarchy root or null.
Ecaps discard needs no caller lock, uses runqueue lock while extracting shared list, returns unrelated entries, marks target detached and waits for held batches; header variant is empty.

state_machines.text: Claims use none, queueing, queued, dispatching: none and dispatching mean owned elsewhere, queued needs sequence match and ownership, move retries, queueing waits; success routes local locally else generically with slice and state-clear modifiers; mismatches abandon silently.

Retry restarts selection, keep retains incumbent with refill, else local head is taken; higher-priority aborts unless forced; empty-slice head warns once then refills; wrappers drop pinning then defer sync waits; core dispatch skips when in flight, runs foreign work directly and retries when lock dropped.
Entry enables tracking and refreshes affinity when identifier handling does not apply and callback exists; exit disables except untracked handoff to parent; priority and post-entry notices are empty.

structs.text: User surface exposes five read-only globals for state, switch-all, rejected count and hotplug and enable sequences as one set, plus per-scheduler operations name and per-event counters with one line per event.

Tasks hold holder, scheduler pointer, atomic op-state with sequence, flags, slice, weight and deferred attributes; runqueues hold local queue with counts, lists, online, dispatch, balance and tick markers, kick counter and sync progress; queues hold identifier, lock and linkage; contexts hold target, counts and per-entry fields; shards hold masks.
